$comment: Shared table for OSCALToken / oscalToken. Read by both converters/oscal-to-hdf/go/oscaltoken_test.go and converters/oscal-to-hdf/typescript/oscaltoken.test.ts so the two implementations are asserted against one definition and cannot drift. The non-ASCII cases exist because the first cut delegated to each platform's Unicode tables (Go's unicode package, V8's \p{L}/\p{N}), which are built from different Unicode versions and disagree on 4657 code points. The encoder now keeps an explicit ASCII set, so every non-ASCII character collapses to '_' identically in both languages.

cases.name: CIS dotted number gets a prefix
empty stays empty for the caller to guard
collapsed leading char is itself a legal lead
collapsed leading digit needs no extra prefix
astral character collapses to one underscore per code point
